title: Moving Into My First Apartment Alone
creator: Lena Fischer
description:
First apartment, no roommates, one very small kitchen. Come move in with me!

Apartment links (rug, lamp, shelves) in the pinned comment.
Playlist: My first year living alone

sentences.t: This video is sponsored by Nestbox, and honestly the timing could not have been better.
Nestbox rents you sturdy plastic moving crates, they drop them off at your old place and pick them up at the new one when you're done.
No buying cardboard, no tape, no boxes collapsing on the stairs with all your plates inside.
They stack, they have lids, and they come with labels so you actually know which one has the kettle.
If you're moving soon, go to nestbox.co/lena to get your first week of crates half price.
Okay hi, welcome, we are moving today!
This is my first apartment where I live completely alone, no roommates, no landlord upstairs, just me.
I'm a little terrified and a lot excited.
We're starting at the old place, which I shared with two girls from university for three years.
It's honestly a bit sad seeing my room empty, there are still marks on the wall from my posters.
My dad came to help, say hi, Dad.
He says hi, he's carrying the heavy stuff because I bribed him with lunch.
The new place is only fifteen minutes away, so we're doing three trips in his car.
Okay, we made it, and this is the building.
It's an old brick building with a really tiny elevator that fits me and maybe one box.
I'm on the fourth floor, so we will be taking a lot of tiny elevator rides today.
Here's the door, here's my key, and oh my gosh, my own apartment.
So you walk in and there's a little hallway with hooks for coats.
On the left is the bathroom, which is small but it has a window, which I was weirdly obsessed with when I viewed it.
Then this is the main room, which is the living room and the bedroom at the same time.
The ceilings are really high, there's this big window looking out over the courtyard, and the floors are old wood.
And over here, the kitchen, which is basically one wall.
Two hot plates, a tiny oven, and about one meter of counter.
I'm going to have to get very creative with storage.
First thing I unpack is always the kettle, because you can't do anything without tea.
Then the bed, because if I don't build the bed first I will end up sleeping on the floor tonight.
Dad and I built the frame in about forty minutes, with only one argument about the instructions.
He was right, I hate that he was right.
Okay, it's evening now, Dad's gone home, and I've been unpacking for hours.
I put up a curtain to split the bed area from the living area, and it makes such a difference.
There's a rug I found at a flea market last month, and a floor lamp that makes everything feel warm.
The books went on a shelf by the window, and yes, they're sorted by color, I know, I'm sorry.
Dinner tonight is pasta, cooked on one hot plate, eaten sitting on the floor because I don't have a table yet.
And honestly, it's the best pasta I've ever had, because it's my pasta in my kitchen.
It's really quiet without roommates.
A little lonely, maybe, but in a good way, if that makes sense.
Next week I'll do a full apartment tour once everything is put away and I've bought a table.
Thank you for coming along on moving day, goodnight from my new home.
